notes: The conceptual list treats several internal state or control paths as separate assets even where the RTL also carries them in the aggregate ctrl_o record; the record port is reported as the boundary structural asset under the control-record rule.

points.reason: debug_ctrl.run is clocked into and out of debug mode, drives ctrl_o.cpu_debug, and selects debug entry and exit behavior.
This generate block only uses debug_ctrl.run to form trigger signals; it does not itself expose, change, or block the stored debug state.
irq_dbg_i is ANDed into debug_ctrl.trig_halt, so an injected or held request creates a debug halt event.
The debug-halt trigger is stored in trap_ctrl.irq_buf and can therefore cause a selected debug trap.
trap_ctrl.irq_buf participates in priority selection of trap_ctrl.cause, redirecting execution to debug handling.
The configured trigger comparison produces hwtrig_match from trigger settings, the program-flow address, and the fired state.
A matching trigger can set hwtrig_fired, recording activation and affecting subsequent trigger behavior.
hwtrig_match starts a debug-trigger path and keeps the engine in dispatch instead of accepting ordinary execution.
hwtrig_start becomes a debug trigger when debug mode is not already active.
Machine and fast interrupt inputs are sampled into irq_pnd and filtered into irq_buf for trap handling.
Buffered interrupt requests select trap_ctrl.cause and can redirect or repeatedly preempt execution.
Instruction and protection faults are copied into trap_ctrl.instr_be and used as exception indications.
Fault indications are latched in trap_ctrl.exc_buf and later cause exception handling.
Buffered exception indications select the trap cause and redirect control flow.
The completion input is required to leave EX_ALU_WAIT and enable writeback; withholding it stalls the operation.
The load/store wait input is tested in EX_MEM_RSP and prevents return to dispatch while asserted.
frontend_i.halted and trap_ctrl.wakeup select sleep_mode, which is stored and returned as ctrl_o.cpu_sleep.
The combinational engine decodes instruction state into ALU, coprocessor, immediate, and writeback controls.
The synchronous block stores the decoded controls before they are driven externally.
The control output carries the execution and writeback commands; corruption or suppression changes execution or prevents completion.
The engine decodes load/store request, direction, atomic, and fence controls from instruction and state.
The synchronous block stores the memory controls before they are driven to the memory subsystem.
The control output carries memory request, direction, atomic, fence, write-enable, and privilege commands.
The engine creates CSR read and write commands and selects the CSR operation.
The CSR write command controls which CSR state is modified.
The control output carries CSR write-enable, read-enable, address, and write-data commands.
CSR state and extension data are selected into csr.rdata and returned through csr_rdata_o.
The output directly exposes the CSR readback word, so it can disclose, corrupt, or withhold the returned value.
The CSR write and trap paths update the stored privilege state.
The effective privilege value is selected from stored privilege state and a debug-mode override.
The effective privilege value crosses the boundary in processor and load/store control fields.
debug_ctrl.run selects machine privilege as an override of the stored privilege level.
Trap, reset, and fetch acknowledgements are selected from pending traps, branches, and frontend validity.
Trap entry clears or gates buffered exceptions, changing whether the frontend and execution flow continue.
The output carries fetch acknowledgement, fetch reset, fence, and trap-entry commands that can redirect or stop instruction processing.
The branch decision controls if_reset and the next program address, so it can redirect instruction processing.
